                    ### Question
                    A six year-old female presents for evaluation of dry skin, fatigue, sensitivity to cold and constipation. The patient’s mother recalls that the patient had surgery to remove a “benign mass” at the base of her tongue 3 months ago because of trouble swallowing. What was the likely cause of the surgically removed mass?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Maternal Diabetes Mellitus
opb. Radiation exposure
opc. Iodine deficiency
opd. Failed caudal migration of the thyroid gland
ope. Failed fusion of the palatine shelves with the nasal septum

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms of dry skin, fatigue, sensitivity to cold, and constipation are indicative of hypothyroidism, which can be associated with ectopic thyroid tissue. The benign mass at the base of the tongue is likely a remnant of thyroid tissue due to failed caudal migration of the thyroid gland during development. This aligns with the consensus that ectopic thyroid tissue can occur when the thyroid does not descend properly. While iodine deficiency can lead to thyroid dysfunction, it is less likely to be the direct cause of the mass in this case. Therefore, the most plausible explanation for the surgically removed mass is failed caudal migration of the thyroid gland.
